:::{#thm-epe-split-noise}
#### The pMSE of a prediction is the pMSE of the mean estimate plus the noise variance

Fix a covariate value $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
The **noise** is $\noise \eqdef \newoutvar - \truemeanfnf{\predvar}$.
It is the [deviation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean)
of the new outcome $\newoutvar$ from its [population mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) given $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
That population mean is the [mean function](#def-mean-function) value $\truemeanfnf{\predvar}$.
So $\newoutvar = \truemeanfnf{\predvar} + \noise$.
The noise has population mean $0$.
Its [population variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) is $\varpar \eqdef \Var{\noise}$, which we take to be finite.

Suppose that the new pair $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$
is drawn from the same population as the observations in the random [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$.
Suppose also that it is [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) of $\trainset$.

Then, given $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
the [expected squared prediction error](#def-epe) (ESPE) of $\predvalf{\predvar}$
is the sum of two terms.
The first is the [irreducible error](#def-irreducible-error) $\varpar$.
The second is the [expected squared estimation error](estimation.qmd#def-mse) (ESEE) of $\predvalf{\predvar}$
as an [estimator](estimation.qmd#def-estimator) of $\truemeanfnf{\predvar}$:

$$
\ESPE{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \varpar + \ESEE{\estmeanf{\predvar}}.
$$ {#eq-epe-split-noise}

:::

::: proof
This is @sol-epe-split-noise.
:::
